models.observations: The square overhead bunker, dark heap and long diagonal feed belt separate coal from the open-legged Mine and stepped GoldMine at 64 pixels. The stack clears the bunker rim, the belt lands on a masonry foot, and the shed door faces the open apron. Rust brick with a dark rim, pale masonry with an orange belt, and a bronze rim on reddish paving distinguish Industrial, Modern and Renaissance. At LOD2 the pile is simpler, but its raised storage bay and incline keep the same profile. Validated LOD triangle counts were 902/528/238.

A bright enclosed incline runs from the ground-level footing to the rim of the elevated coal bin. The dark heap remains visible against the pale bin wall, with the rear blue feed housing and stepped doorway giving separate upper and lower work areas. The capped housing and bin lip shift from silver to gold between Information and Ascension. At 64 pixels all three meshes retain the strong diagonal and squared bunker that distinguish this operation from the hoist and wash beds. Validated LOD triangle counts were 956/628/294.

Three timber-rimmed blue wash beds descend from the short stone header past a low brown work shed. Gold flecks track the riffles in the front bed and an ochre fitting sits under the header. The squat Iron silhouette is easy to pick out beside the generic Mine's tall, narrow timber frame. At 64 pixels the broad steps carry the identity at every LOD, including the simplified top basin and plainer bottom bed on LOD2. Validated LOD triangle counts were 1031/586/242.

Two square pillars carry a red-edged header over three descending blue troughs. A small fitting hangs in the upper gap and a pitched shed marks the near corner. The white stone and red shed of Classical give way to dark Medieval paving and roofing, then warm tan Renaissance stone. Across the three LODs the open upper span and terraces stay clear at 64 pixels, distinct from the peaked generic hoist and the Renaissance coal bunker. Validated LOD triangle counts were 1079/686/302.

A horizontal, banded sorting drum on two piers crowns the three blue wash beds. Its end hub projects clearly at full size. Rust masonry and dark iron in Industrial shift to pale supports and orange drum bands in Modern. The bands simplify to the ends at LOD2, while the cylinder, stair-step profile and lower shed still distinguish the gold works from the generic hoist and coal bin at 64 pixels. Validated LOD triangle counts were 1299/770/266.

Paired inward-curving stone arms frame a cyan crystal above the washing terraces. Three bright water surfaces and a low side shed stay visible even as the tiny gold riffle details simplify. The cap remains blue in Information, while the ledges, crystal seat and right-hand trim turn gold in Ascension. The forked crown and stepped front read at 64 pixels on all three meshes beside the open Mine and the inclined coal feeder. Validated LOD triangle counts were 1019/602/306.
